_readme: Overlay applied on top of the machine-extracted FSM rows for the 2003 C5.
supersessions  - a GM bulletin that REVISED the FSM value. The FSM number
is real, published, and WRONG. Without this overlay the
site would serve a stale value that looks maximally
corroborations - independent sources that agree with the FSM value. Two or
more independent agreements promote a row from tier B to A.
Every entry cites a retrievable URL. Nothing here was inferred or estimated;
where sources disagreed the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved.

sources.title: GM Bulletin 05-03-08-004 — Revised Ball Joint Stud Nut Tightening Specifications (1997-2005 Corvette)
sources.note: Revises the upper and lower ball joint stud nut specs in the Front and Rear Suspension sub-sections of the service manual. The bulletin does not reprint the prior values.

sources.title: GM Bulletin 07-06-01-002 (Doc ID 1912616) — New Connecting Rod Bolt Torque Specification
sources.note: Applies to 1997-2008 Chevrolet Corvette (excluding LS7). Second-pass value increased from 75 degrees to 85 degrees, using the J 45059 Angle Meter.

sources.title: GM Bulletin 02-03-10-008 — Recommended Wheel Nut Torque Specifications (2003 Corvette)
sources.note: Informational, not a revision. 2003 Corvette: 5 x M12 x 1.5, BCD 120.65 mm, 19 mm hex, service torque 140 N-m (100 lb ft).

sources.title: Elite Engineering — C5 Torque Values (David Farmer community spec sheet)
sources.note: FSM-derived transcription. Pre-2005 vintage, so it carries the ORIGINAL ball joint specs.

sources.title: Corvette Web Central — C5 Corvette Torque Values
sources.note: Same base document as the Elite sheet but a post-TSB vintage, so it carries the REVISED ball joint specs. Not independent of Elite, but the delta between them is a clean before/after snapshot of TSB 05-03-08-004.

sources.title: Van Steel — Torque Specs (C5/C6)
sources.note: CAUTION: interleaves OE specs with Van Steel / QA1 / Wilwood aftermarket values in one table. Only rows marked factory, or matching another source, are usable as OE corroboration.

sources.title: Summit Racing — Chevrolet LS Gen. 3 Aluminum Block Torque Specs
sources.note: Covers LS1/LS6/LM4/L33 specifically, with bolt lengths called out.

supersessions.matchName: Lower Control Arm Ball Joint Stud Nut
supersessions.note: Bulletin 05-03-08-004 revised this spec for 1997-2005. Corroborated independently by the Corvette Web Central sheet and by Van Steel, which both publish +180 degrees for the lower ball joints.

supersessions.matchName: Lower Control Arm Ball Joint Stud Nut
supersessions.note: Bulletin 05-03-08-004 revised this spec for 1997-2005. The manual's 3 1/2 flats second pass is withdrawn.

supersessions.matchName: Upper Control Arm Ball Joint Stud Nut
supersessions.note: Bulletin 05-03-08-004 revised this spec. For 1997-2004 the final torque pass is REMOVED and replaced by a 250 degree turn. 2005 cars use 30 N·m (22 lb ft) + 225 degrees instead.

supersessions.matchName: Upper Control Arm Ball Joint Stud Nut
supersessions.note: Bulletin 05-03-08-004 revised this spec. For 1997-2004 the manual's final 55 N·m (41 lb ft) pass is REMOVED; the 250 degree turn becomes the final pass. 2005 cars use 30 N·m (22 lb ft) + 195 degrees instead.

Bulletin 07-06-01-002 increased the second pass from 75 to 85 degrees for 1997-2008 Corvette (excluding LS7). Corroborated by Summit Racing and Michigan Motorsports. Note that many community spec sheets still publish the superseded 75 degree value.

corroborations.note: GM bulletin gives the same service torque and the fastener spec: 5 x M12 x 1.5, 19 mm hex.

Front Brake Caliper Mounting Bracket Bolt
corroborations.note: Four sources reproduce 125 lb ft, which suggests a shared transcription lineage rather than true independence. 175 N·m converts to 129 lb ft, so the printed pair is internally loose.

corroborations.value: 22 lb ft / +90° / +90° long M11, +50° medium M11, 22 lb ft M8
corroborations.note: Summit lists bolt lengths explicitly: M11 x 155.5 gets 22 lb ft then 90 then 90; M11 x 101.0 gets 22 lb ft then 50; M8 x 46.0 gets 22 lb ft.

_aliasesReadme: Slang and common names that do NOT appear anywhere in GM's wording, so no
amount of lexical or synonym matching can reach the record without them.
'Lug nut' is the clearest case: the FSM says 'Wheel Nuts' and never 'lug',
which let 'Steering Wheel Nut' tie with the real wheel nut record.
These are seeded by hand; the app also learns aliases when you pick from an
abstain list. Aliases only affect RETRIEVAL — they never touch a value.

singleUse.reason: Stock-style LS cylinder head bolts are torque-to-yield and must never be reused.
Torque-to-yield. Any fastener finished by an angle spec stretches permanently.

singleUse.matchName: Crankshaft Bearing Cap Bolts - Inner Bolts
Crankshaft Bearing Cap Studs - Outer Studs

singleUse.reason: Torque-to-yield. The installation pass uses the OLD bolt; a NEW bolt must then be fitted for the 37 lb ft + 140 degree sequence.

disagreements.assessment: The FSM value is corroborated by two further sources. The Van Steel page covers 1997-2013 and mixes aftermarket coilover hardware, so its outlier is most likely not an OE spec.

notIngested.item: Seat belt retractor and anchor torques circulating on CorvetteForum
notIngested.reason: The originating thread's author states a member 'thought' these were right and 'wasn't sure', and the thread closes without confirmation. Restraint-system fastener — not propagated without a primary source.

notIngested.item: Steering intermediate shaft lower coupling bolt
notIngested.reason: Two retrievable forum posts say 25 lb ft with threadlocker; an unretrievable source claims 37 lb ft and single-use. Unresolved contradiction on a steering fastener — neither value ingested.

notIngested.item: Steering gear / rack-to-crossmember bolts (74 lb ft)
notIngested.reason: Single uncorroborated forum post on a steering fastener.

notIngested.item: Exhaust manifold bolt revision (GM 06-06-01-026, 10 N·m then 20 N·m with threadlocker)
notIngested.reason: Quoted second-hand on a forum; primary bulletin text could not be retrieved. The FSM's 15 then 25 N·m is retained and this is noted as unconfirmed.

notIngested.item: Crankshaft balancer bolt at 24 lb ft (My Pro Street)
notIngested.reason: Off by roughly 10x against six other sources. Physically implausible for crank balancer retention.
